title: Évariste Galois — Mathematical Works (1897): Source-Faithful English Translation and GPT-Annotated Edition
description:
Open the source-faithful English translation or download it directly.

Open the GPT-annotated English edition or download it directly.

Both PDFs belong to this same English record, version 2026-08-14 en-r3, and exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21935485; neither reader has a separate DOI. The first is a direct, source-based English translation without modern GPT annotations. It retains Galois's text, Émile Picard's Introduction, the 1897/Tannery editorial material, historical footnotes, formulas, contents, figures, colophon, and honest page topology, including historically defective claims as printed. The second uses the same translated corpus and adds the polished, human-readable GPT critical apparatus: corrections, qualifications, counterexamples, witness differences, and evidence-linked editorial notes. The complete substantive coverage is PDF001–PDF096 / W01–W11, with 11 components and 587 aligned English segments.

The predecessor annotated edition remains immutable at exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21926209. This release is tagged v2026.08.14-en-r3 in the existing repository. Historical author: Évariste Galois. Edition identity and maintenance: Manuscript Typesetting Project. Post-P13 research and mathematical certificates were supplied by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in Pro mode. English translation, source-faithful projection, critical integration, DOI release engineering, and independent QA were supplied by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in Ultra mode. No human translator is asserted.

Stable English concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21924301. French source-language concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21923856. Global project: 10.5281/zenodo.20393488. Repository: github.com/KokunoYumeto/evariste-galois-en.

DataCite intent: the English concept IsTranslationOf the French concept, and the French concept HasTranslation the English concept. Because Zenodo does not currently expose those relation values, this record uses isDerivedFrom the French concept as the machine-readable fallback. The separate isPartOf relation identifies the global project. Exact directions are preserved in the repository and relation sidecar.

Rights: this is an open-access mixed-rights aggregate, so the record uses Zenodo's other-open classification rather than claiming one unconditional license over every byte. Project-owned translation, editorial apparatus, typesetting, metadata, scripts, manifests, and QA are dedicated under CC0 1.0 only to the extent owned by the Manuscript Typesetting Project. The 1897 historical text is identified as public-domain source material. Third-party scans, catalogue metadata, witness artifacts, and the separately packaged French sibling retain their own source-specific status and are not relicensed. The per-file rules and downstream obligations are stated in RIGHTS_AND_LICENSING.md.

Release closure uses source replay, model/agent checks, deterministic builds, rendered inspection, hashes, and honest unresolved disclosure; no human-review gate is imposed.
